Global Exchange Program: Studying in Bonn for a semester or year
The Global Exchange Program opens a path for students at the University of Bonn’s partner universities outside Europe to study for a year or a semester at the University of Bonn. Nearly 100 different degree programs are offered, as well as a diverse range of courses to help program participants master the German language.
Program Objectives
The Global Exchange Program was founded to provide international students worldwide with the chance to spend a portion of their studies (one or two semesters) in Bonn. It offers students an unparalleled opportunity to expand their intercultural competencies while still studying for a bachelor’s or master’s degree by integrating them into daily life at a German university and the larger German society. Application and Preparation — University of Bonn
de
en
Application and Preparation
You have decided to study in Bonn with the Global Exchange Program? Here you will find all the information and forms for your application as well as tips to prepare for your time studying abroad.
Who can apply?
To apply for the Global Exchange Program scheme, you must meet the following requirements:
You must be currently studying at one of the University of Bonn’s partner universities (your nationality is not important).
You are interested in studying at the University of Bonn for one or two semesters.
Bachelor’s degree students: you must have completed at least the first year of your degree program before you begin studying in Bonn.
Students can apply in any academic discipline (excepting medicine and dentistry). Candidates will be selected by their home universities based on a variety of criteria, including academic performance, interests, motivation and language skills.

Niveau de langue requis
Niveau de langue requis pour étudier dans le DEUF
Pour étudier dans le programme DEUF, vous devez justifier d’un niveau de français:
Niveau B1 minimum obligatoire pour les cours de Langues, Humanités, Lettres & Sociétés et iaelyon School of Management.
Niveau B2 obligatoire pour les enseignements en Droit, Science Politique et Philosophie
Niveau C1 pour les enseignements d’Information & Communication.
